questions.question:
In namespace `rbac-ex04`:

1. Create a ServiceAccount named `dev-sa`.
2. Create a Role named `pod-manager` that grants:
   - `get`, `list`, `watch`, `create`, `delete` on `pods`
   - `get`, `list` on `services`
   - `patch` on the `deployments/scale` **subresource** (API group `apps`)
3. Create a RoleBinding named `dev-pod-access` that binds Role `pod-manager` to ServiceAccount `dev-sa`.
4. Create a ClusterRole named `node-viewer` granting `get`, `list` on `nodes`, and a ClusterRoleBinding named `dev-node-access` binding it to `dev-sa`.

You can verify the result with `kubectl auth can-i <verb> <resource> -n rbac-ex04 --as=system:serviceaccount:rbac-ex04:dev-sa` (for the scale subresource: `kubectl auth can-i patch deployments --subresource=scale ...`). The ServiceAccount must NOT gain any permissions outside the `rbac-ex04` namespace (listing nodes cluster-wide is the only exception).

verification.description: ServiceAccount dev-sa can list pods in rbac-ex04
ServiceAccount dev-sa can patch the deployments/scale subresource
dev-sa cannot delete deployments and cannot list pods outside rbac-ex04
dev-sa can list nodes via the ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding

questions.question:
In namespace `sidecar-ex02`, create a Deployment named `logger` with **1 replica** and label `app=logger` that uses the native sidecar pattern:

1. Main container `app` (image `busybox:1.36`) that appends a line to `/var/log/app/app.log` every 3 seconds:
`sh -c 'while true; do echo "$(date) - app running" >> /var/log/app/app.log; sleep 3; done'`
2. An **init container** named `log-agent` (image `busybox:1.36`) with `restartPolicy: Always` - that is what makes it a native sidecar - running `sh -c 'tail -F /var/log/app/app.log'`
3. Both containers must mount the same `emptyDir` volume named `log-volume` at `/var/log/app`.

Wait until the Pod is Ready with both containers running so the sidecar streams the application log.

verification.description: Pod template has init container log-agent with restartPolicy Always and image busybox:1.36
EmptyDir volume log-volume is mounted at /var/log/app in both containers
Deployment is Ready and the log-agent sidecar container is running

questions.question:
In namespace `ingress-ex19` two Services already exist: `web-service` (port `80`) and `api-service` (port `8080`), backed by the Deployments `web-app` and `api-app`. A TLS Secret named `api-tls-cert` has also been created.

Create a single Ingress named `web-ingress` in `ingress-ex19`:

1. Set `ingressClassName` to `nginx`.
2. Terminate TLS for host `api.example.com` using the Secret `api-tls-cert`.
3. Rule for host `web.example.com`: path `/` (type `Prefix`) routed to Service `web-service` port `80`.
4. Rule for host `api.example.com`: path `/api` (type `Prefix`) routed to Service `api-service` port `8080`.

verification.description: Ingress web-ingress exists with ingressClassName nginx
TLS section uses secret api-tls-cert for host api.example.com
web.example.com / (Prefix) routes to web-service:80
api.example.com /api (Prefix) routes to api-service:8080

questions.question:
In namespace `resource-tuning` a ResourceQuota named `compute-quota` limits total container requests to `1` CPU and `2Gi` memory (and at most 10 pods).

The Deployment `web` (3 replicas, image `nginx:1.27`, label `app=web`) declares requests of `1200m` CPU and `1Gi` memory per container - even a single pod asks for more CPU than the whole quota allows, so the ReplicaSet cannot create any pods and the API rejects them with `exceeded quota: compute-quota` (check the ReplicaSet events).

Fix the Deployment so all 3 replicas run:

1. Keep declaring both `requests.cpu` and `requests.memory` on the container - do not remove them, and do not delete or edit the ResourceQuota.
2. Lower the per-container requests so that the total for 3 replicas fits within the quota.
3. Wait until all 3 pods are Running.

verification.description: Deployment web runs exactly 3 ready replicas
Every container still declares positive requests.cpu and requests.memory
Total requests of the 3 pods fit within the quota (<= 1000m CPU and <= 2Gi memory)
ResourceQuota compute-quota is unchanged (requests.cpu=1, requests.memory=2Gi, pods=10)

questions.question:
In namespace `wffc-ex25`:

1. Create a StorageClass named `local-wffc` with provisioner `rancher.io/local-path` and `volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer`.
2. Create a PersistentVolumeClaim named `local-pvc` (1Gi, `ReadWriteOnce`, storageClassName `local-wffc`). It will stay `Pending` - that is expected until a Pod consumes it.
3. Create a Deployment named `app` (1 replica, image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`, label `app=app`) that mounts `local-pvc` at `/data`.

Once the Pod is scheduled the claim should bind and the Pod must run.

verification.description: StorageClass local-wffc uses rancher.io/local-path with WaitForFirstConsumer binding
PVC local-pvc is 1Gi ReadWriteOnce on local-wffc and is Bound
Deployment app mounts local-pvc at /data and is Ready

questions.question:
Node `k3d-cluster-agent-1` needs maintenance.

1. Cordon the node so it is marked `SchedulingDisabled`.
2. Drain it. The drain must succeed despite DaemonSet-managed pods and pods that hold data on the node's filesystem - use the appropriate `kubectl drain` flags.
3. Confirm the pods of the Job `drain-marker` in namespace `drain-ex08` (created by the lab setup on that node) have been evicted - no `drain-marker` pods should remain.
4. Uncordon the node.
5. Scale the Deployment `drain-demo` in namespace `drain-ex08` from 2 to 4 replicas and confirm the new Pods also land on the now-schedulable `k3d-cluster-agent-1`.

verification.description: Node k3d-cluster-agent-1 is schedulable (not cordoned)
drain-marker Job pods were evicted (none remain)
Deployment drain-demo runs 4 ready replicas
At least one drain-demo pod runs on k3d-cluster-agent-1

questions.question:
In namespace `rollout-ex06`:

1. Create a Deployment named `webapp` (3 replicas, image `nginx:1.27`, label `app=webapp`) with strategy `RollingUpdate`, `maxSurge: 1`, `maxUnavailable: 0`.
2. Record the change cause with the annotation `kubernetes.io/change-cause` = `initial deploy nginx:1.27`.
3. Update the image to `nginx:1.28` and record change cause `update to nginx:1.28` (the annotation lives on the Deployment object itself, so you will need `--overwrite`).
4. Wait for the rollout to finish, then roll back to the previous revision so the Deployment runs `nginx:1.27` again.

verification.description: Strategy is RollingUpdate with maxSurge 1, maxUnavailable 0 and 3 replicas
Deployment runs nginx:1.27, rollout history has at least 2 revisions and the intermediate nginx:1.28 ReplicaSet exists
Annotation kubernetes.io/change-cause is set on the Deployment
All 3 replicas are ready

questions.question:
In namespace `cron-ex21` create a CronJob named `db-cleanup`:

1. Schedule: `*/5 * * * *`
2. `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`
3. Job template: container name `cleanup`, image `busybox:1.37`, command `sh -c 'echo cleanup; date'`, `backoffLimit: 2`, `restartPolicy: Never`
4. Trigger it once manually: create a Job named `db-cleanup-manual` from the CronJob (`kubectl create job db-cleanup-manual --from=cronjob/db-cleanup`) and wait for it to complete successfully.

verification.description: CronJob db-cleanup has schedule */5 * * * * and concurrencyPolicy Forbid
Job template uses busybox:1.37, backoffLimit 2, restartPolicy Never and the cleanup command
Job db-cleanup-manual exists and completed successfully

questions.question:
In namespace `prod` the Deployment `payments-api` is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff. The container (named `app`, image `busybox:1.36`) exits with status 1 because it expects a configuration file at `/etc/app/app.env` that does not exist.

Fix it without changing the Deployment's command:

1. Create a ConfigMap named `payments-config` in `prod` with a key `app.env` whose value contains the line `DB_HOST=postgres.prod.svc.cluster.local`.
2. Mount the ConfigMap into the Deployment at `/etc/app` so the file appears at `/etc/app/app.env`.
3. Wait until the Pod is Running and Ready.

verification.description: ConfigMap payments-config contains key app.env with DB_HOST=postgres.prod.svc.cluster.local
Deployment mounts the ConfigMap at /etc/app
Pod is Ready and /etc/app/app.env exists inside the container

questions.question:
In namespace `job-ex21` create a Job named `cleanup-job`:

1. Image `busybox:1.37` running the command `echo "Cleanup complete"`.
2. `restartPolicy: Never`
3. Run it three times successfully: `completions: 3` with `parallelism: 1` (the three runs happen one after another).
4. Wait until the Job reports 3/3 completions.

verification.description: Job has completions 3, parallelism 1 and restartPolicy Never
Job completed with 3 successful runs
Job command echoes 'Cleanup complete'
